claims.text: The starting AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy has a uniform, fine lamellar FCC/B2 duplex microstructure.
The starting lamellar structure is an as-cast structure without post-processing.
The as-cast alloy has insufficient strength and plasticity for demanding industrial fastener applications.
An approximately 8% cold-rolling reduction followed by low-temperature annealing is a suitable thermomechanical intervention.
The cited prior work specifically supports an 8% cold-rolling reduction.
The proposed thermomechanical treatment will refine the duplex lamellar microstructure and optimize FCC/B2 phase spacing and distribution.
Reduced lamellar spacing will increase interphase-boundary density.
The increased phase-boundary density will impede dislocation motion.
The increased phase-boundary density will impede crack propagation.
Two-hierarchical constraint and self-generated microcrack-arrest mechanisms improve the strength-ductility synergy of AlCoCrFeNi2.1.
The treatment will increase tensile and yield strengths relative to the as-cast alloy.
The treatment will retain or improve ductility relative to the as-cast alloy.
The treatment will improve room-temperature creep resistance.
The treatment will improve corrosion resistance.
Improved corrosion resistance will result from enhanced protective-oxide formation and a more uniform microstructure.
The predicted treatment benefits apply from room temperature to approximately 700 degrees Celsius.
The predicted benefits apply under long-term static and dynamic loading and in corrosive environments.
Significant deviations in rolling reduction or annealing temperature and time may alter the treatment effect.

contradictions.description: The treatment is said to be performed under ambient conditions, but the intervention includes a low-temperature anneal, which necessarily entails an elevated treatment temperature unless 'ambient conditions' refers only to the laboratory atmosphere.
